response:
## The problem

Our team of twelve has drifted into long-lived feature branches, some open for three or more weeks. Merges have become dreading events instead of routine ones. Last month's payments-refactor branch required two full days of conflict resolution and produced a regression that shipped to production because nobody had tested the merged result end-to-end. Integration risk is being deferred, not eliminated, and it's landing all at once, late, when it's most expensive to fix.

## The proposal

Move to trunk-based development: everyone commits to main at least once a day, features ship dark behind flags, and branches live for hours, not weeks. Concretely:

- All new work is feature-flagged so incomplete code can sit in main without being user-visible.
- Branches are capped at roughly one day; anything longer gets split into smaller commits.
- CI on main must stay green at all times, with a fast rollback path (revert or flag-off) as the default response to a broken build.
- Code review shifts to smaller, more frequent diffs rather than one large review at merge time.
- We pilot this on one squad for three weeks before rolling it out team-wide.

This trades big, rare merge pain for small, constant integration discipline — which is easier to reason about and catches problems while they're still cheap to fix.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: without long branches, half-finished features are visible in main, and a careless flag or a forgotten cleanup could leak unfinished work to users or clutter the codebase with permanent scaffolding. This isn't a hypothetical — teams that adopt trunk-based development without discipline around flag hygiene end up with worse technical debt than the branching problem they solved. The honest answer is that this only works if we also commit to a flag lifecycle: naming conventions, an owner per flag, and a standing backlog item to remove flags within a sprint of full rollout. Without that commitment, I'd agree this proposal isn't worth adopting.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
